content.title: About
content.content: Cake, cupcake and gingerbread are baked goods made from flour, sugar, eggs and fats, often flavored with spices, fruit or chocolate. Cake is usually layered and frosted, cupcake is denser and single‑serve, while gingerbread is a traditional spiced cookie popular in colder seasons.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Cakes have cultural variations: in Russia a "honey cake" is served at weddings, in Japan a "sofu cake" is a specialty.
Cupcakes earned the nickname "American" due to their surge in popularity in the United States in the early 20th century.
Gingerbread originated in medieval Europe as a medicinal confection made with ginger and honey.
In the United States, over 200 million gingerbread cookies are sold each Christmas season.
Traditional German "Lebkuchen" is considered the ancestor of modern gingerbread.

items.title: Energy source
items.content: The carbohydrate content in cake, cupcake and gingerbread provides a quick source of energy.

items.title: Rich in antioxidants
items.content: Spices such as ginger, cinnamon and clove contain polyphenols that help combat free radicals.

items.title: Supports digestion
items.content: Ginger in gingerbread stimulates gastric secretions and can aid digestion.

items.title: B‑vitamin content
items.content: Eggs and whole‑grain flour in cakes and cupcakes supply vitamins B1, B2 and B6.

items.title: Minerals
items.content: Flour and nuts, often added to recipes, provide magnesium, iron and zinc.

items.title: High sugar content
items.content: Large portions may raise blood glucose levels and contribute to weight gain.

items.title: Allergens
items.content: Cakes and cupcakes frequently contain nuts, dairy and eggs, which can trigger allergic reactions.

items.title: Trans fats
items.content: Using margarine or partially hydrogenated oils can introduce trans fats, which are harmful to heart health.

items.title: Gluten content
items.content: People with celiac disease or gluten sensitivity should choose gluten‑free versions.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve cake in slices, often with fruit or berry sauce. Cupcakes are convenient as a snack, halved if desired. Gingerbread is commonly enjoyed with tea, glazed or dusted with powdered sugar.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep baked goods in an airtight container at room temperature for up to 3 days. For longer storage, refrigerate (up to 1 week) or freeze (up to 3 months). Gingerbread stays best in a dry place to stay crisp.
